subject: MAP: Verity pilot - unit economics sanity check & close cadence
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morrow <elena@verityhealthtech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-02T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: Verity pilot - unit economics sanity check & close cadence

Hi Elena — attaching the initial MAP worksheet with our unit-econ assumptions (verity-map-econ-v1.xlsx). Key bullets so you can scan quickly:

- Tokens per user (pilot): we modeled 1,200 tokens/session avg (600 prompt / 600 completion).
- Baseline model: open-model-5B quantized to 8-bit; per-token runtime cost assumes optimized kernels and batching.
- Tokens / $: baseline yields ~28,000 tokens / USD under expected batching and caching (see sheet Tab "Units").
- Caching: prefix caching enabled for 30% of sessions (session-level KV reuse for 10–60s TTL) — reduces expected billed tokens by ~15% in our traffic simulation.
- Batching assumptions: we assumed 40ms extra latency budget for batching, 12 request batching window, effective concurrency 18 at peak.
- Dedicated vs hosted: numbers assume hosted inference with smart routing; we included an alternate column for dedicated-reserved pricing.

Asks for your team: please confirm a couple quick inputs so we can lock the MAP econ for procurement:
1) Expected median prompt length (tokens) for the evaluation set (is 600 realistic?),
2) Whether prefix caching is allowed for PHI-containing prompts (we can turn caching off per-tenant if needed),
3) Expected evaluation traffic profile (spikey burst vs steady).

Proposed evaluation + close timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (Dec 11–15): onboarding, sample prompt pass, baseline metrics collection (latency, quality).
- Week 2 (Dec 18–22): A/B eval (no-cache vs prefix-cache) across 5k sessions, cost telemetry live.
- Week 3 (Dec 26–30): Finalize MAP edits + procurement prep; target sign by Jan 5 if acceptance gates met.

If we lock the 15% caching benefit and current batching profile, we can show a conservative tokens/$ improvement of ~18–20% versus no-cache baseline in the pilot. I included a short sensitivity table in the workbook.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync tomorrow if useful.

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0190

Attachment: verity-map-econ-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120kb)

From: Elena Morrow <elena@verityhealthtech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-03T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Verity pilot - unit economics sanity check & close cadence

Hi Karthik — thanks for the deck and the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs before we circulate internally: 

- Prompt length: 600 tokens seems high for our workflows (most clinician lookups average ~150–300). Is the 600 token assumption coming from worst-case long notes?
- Caching & PHI: our security team will require that any cached prefixes are encrypted and have a defined retention policy. Can you confirm whether per-tenant KV TTL and KMS integration are included in the pilot?
- Latency SLO: during the clinician flow, anything >250ms tail will be disruptive. How much headroom do you expect when batching is applied?

Also linking our procurement lead in case they want to see the sensitivity table: procurement@verityhealthtech.com.

If we can get those answers, I can commit to a cross-functional review on Dec 6 and then push the MAP forward.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Verity HealthTech
elena@verityhealthtech.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morrow <elena@verityhealthtech.com>
Date: 2028-12-04T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Verity pilot - unit economics sanity check & close cadence

Karthik / Ben — quick finance note to feed back to Verity before their Dec 6 review. I've annotated the econ assumptions in the attached PDF (econ-assumptions-annotated.pdf). Highlights: 

- Prompt median: we should model 250 tokens median and include a 90th percentile of 1,100 tokens in sensitivity. Recalculate the "typical" tokens/$ using a mixed distribution (70% short, 30% long).
- Quantization: the 8-bit line is fine; we also included a column for 4-bit quantized variant which improves tokens/$ by ~35% but can change quality metrics — note this as optional for Dedicated later.
- Caching: the 15% uplift assumes cacheable prefix rate of 30% and cache hit efficacy of 50% (i.e., half the cached prefixes avoid completion tokens). If Verity's workflows have conservative PHI rules, degrade that to 8–10% and we still show non-trivial savings.
- Batching vs latency: given a 250ms tail SLO target, we recommend a max batching delay of 10ms (shorter window) with slightly lower tokens/$ (~12% uplift vs the 18–20% in Karthik's baseline). We'll call this the low-latency profile.

Action items I recommend for Dec 6 review: 
1) Run a short re-sim that uses median=250, cache-hit-effect=10% (privacy conservative), and low-latency batching window (10ms). Put that sim into Tab "Conservative".
2) Confirm encryption/KMS requirements (Elena: can procurement share a minimal KMS spec?)
3) If those conservative numbers still meet Verity's budget gates, we sign the MAP and proceed to SOW/DSO.

I'm attaching the annotated assumptions. I'll be available to join the Dec 6 call if you want finance-level signoff live.

--
Neha Kapoor
Director, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: econ-assumptions-annotated.pdf (annotated PDF, 45kb)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morrow <elena@verityhealthtech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@verityhealthtech.com
Date: 2028-12-07T16:27:00-08:00
Subject: MAP v2 - conservative econ numbers, evaluation gates, and close cadence

Elena / team — based on Neha's conservative sim I ran this morning, I updated the MAP doc (redwood-map-v2.docx) and summarized the acceptance gates below. Please consider this the version we'll take to procurement.

Key conservative econ numbers (locked for the MAP):
- Modeled median tokens/session: 250 (70% short, 30% long),
- Effective caching uplift (privacy-conservative): 10% tokens saved,
- Batching profile: low-latency 10ms max window (sacrifices some batching efficiency),
- Resulting tokens/$ (conservative): ~21,500 tokens / USD.

Acceptance gates for pilot (must pass to close):
1) Latency: p95 end-to-end <250ms under pilot traffic (low-latency profile).
2) Quality: A/B blind eval shows no meaningful regression on core clinician tasks (pass/fail checklist attached in doc).
3) Security: KV caching obeys per-tenant TTL and KMS encryption (procurement: can you confirm KMS provider & minimal AEs?).
4) Cost: conservative tokens/$ meets Verity's pilot budget threshold for a 3-month pilot.

Evaluation plan & timeframe (updated):
- Dec 11–15: onboarding + baseline metrics (we'll ship an instrumented client and baseline recorder).
- Dec 18–22: 2k session A/B test (low-latency vs no-cache), cost telemetry + quality eval (blind).
- Dec 26–30: internal review and MAP sign-off; target SOW send the week of Jan 2; aim to have signature by Jan 12.

Links: HubSpot deal and DocuSign template are included below. I'll upload the final MAP doc to the shared drive after this note.

If procurement can confirm KMS provider and any retention limits by Dec 9, we'll be fully aligned for the Dec 11 onboarding. Otherwise, we'll proceed with caching disabled for the pilot by default.

Thanks — I'll update the MAP doc in the link and send a short (20m) sync invite for Dec 8 at 10am PT to walk the conservative numbers live.

Regards,
Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-map-v2.docx (MAP doc, ~95kb)
